# Test Harness Templates

Templates for generating test cases from review findings. Each template
targets a specific test framework and produces both a negative test
(reproduces the bad pattern) and a positive test (verifies the fix).

Select the template based on the project's test framework. If the framework
is not listed, adapt the closest template.

---

## pytest (Python)

```python
# test_{finding_id}.py
# Generated by code-review-gate for finding: {pattern_id}
# File: {file_path}:{line_number}

import pytest


class TestReviewFinding_{finding_id}:
    """Regression tests for {pattern_id} in {file_path}."""

    def test_bad_pattern_detected(self):
        """The bad pattern should not be present after fix."""
        # {description}
        # Arrange
        {setup_code}

        # Act
        {action_code}

        # Assert
        {negative_assertion}

    def test_fix_applied(self):
        """The fix should produce correct behavior."""
        # Arrange
        {setup_code}

        # Act
        {fixed_action_code}

        # Assert
        {positive_assertion}
```

## jest (JavaScript/TypeScript)

```javascript
// {finding_id}.test.js
// Generated by code-review-gate for finding: {pattern_id}
// File: {file_path}:{line_number}

describe('{pattern_id} in {file_path}', () => {
  it('should not contain the bad pattern', () => {
    // {description}
    // Arrange
    {setup_code}

    // Act
    {action_code}

    // Assert
    {negative_assertion}
  });

  it('should behave correctly after fix', () => {
    // Arrange
    {setup_code}

    // Act
    {fixed_action_code}

    // Assert
    {positive_assertion}
  });
});
```

---

## go test (Go)

```go
// {finding_id}_test.go
// Generated by code-review-gate for finding: {pattern_id}
// File: {file_path}:{line_number}

package {package_name}

import "testing"

func TestBadPattern_{finding_id}(t *testing.T) {
	// {description}
	// Arrange
	{setup_code}

	// Act
	{action_code}

	// Assert
	{negative_assertion}
}

func TestFixApplied_{finding_id}(t *testing.T) {
	// Arrange
	{setup_code}

	// Act
	{fixed_action_code}

	// Assert
	{positive_assertion}
}
```

---

## rspec (Ruby)

```ruby
# spec/{finding_id}_spec.rb
# Generated by code-review-gate for finding: {pattern_id}
# File: {file_path}:{line_number}

RSpec.describe '{pattern_id} in {file_path}' do
  context 'when the bad pattern is present' do
    it 'should not pass validation' do
      # {description}
      # Arrange
      {setup_code}

      # Act
      {action_code}

      # Assert
      {negative_assertion}
    end
  end

  context 'when the fix is applied' do
    it 'should behave correctly' do
      # Arrange
      {setup_code}

      # Act
      {fixed_action_code}

      # Assert
      {positive_assertion}
    end
  end
end
```

---

## Template Variables

When generating test cases, replace these placeholders:

| Variable | Source |
|---|---|
| `{finding_id}` | Sanitized unique ID for the finding (snake_case) |
| `{pattern_id}` | Pattern ID from review-patterns.md |
| `{file_path}` | File where the finding was detected |
| `{line_number}` | Line number of the finding |
| `{description}` | Human-readable description of the issue |
| `{setup_code}` | Code to set up the test scenario |
| `{action_code}` | Code that triggers the bad pattern |
| `{fixed_action_code}` | Code that demonstrates the correct approach |
| `{negative_assertion}` | Assertion that the bad pattern is absent |
| `{positive_assertion}` | Assertion that the fix works correctly |
| `{package_name}` | Go package name (Go only) |
